setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I already spoke to Kim, of course, you already gave me some ideas from where you're at, where you want to go.' Prospect: 'I don't know if you got any notes there from the previous guy I talked to, but yeah, I spoke to Kim.'

prospect.name: Lance Mardian
prospect.occupation: Full-time independent stock trader; previously ran crews at an ethanol plant for about 15 years until quitting roughly eight months ago
prospect.family_status: Two nieces in California via a younger brother, three nephews locally; father Dan Mardian, 65, once very fit and now overweight and medicated for blood pressure
prospect.training_background: Trained in the gym essentially every day through his twenties and early thirties, including active rest days on the treadmill. Consistency broke down in his mid-thirties and stopped entirely a few years ago. Has thrown a kettlebell around a few times. Wants to combine kettlebells with calisthenics.
prospect.medical: Self-disclosed slight scoliosis — 'very minimal, never needed surgery, never needed a back brace' — which he says leaves him dominantly stronger on the right side than the left. Intermittent right knee ache lasting two to three days at a time; persistent right elbow ache on gripping, which he attributes to game controller use. Formerly took Aleve and ibuprofen regularly at his old job, now stopped. Heart racing after walking up a hill while hunting. Reports significant brain fog over the last year or two. Volunteered that he 'stopped caring' about himself, while explicitly stating he is not depressed.

signals: Self-directed and capable, with a decisive precedent he cited himself: he nearly spent $5,000-$10,000 on an automated trading system, chose to grind it out alone, and succeeded — 'I saved myself that $5,000, $10,000'
Anchored hard to free information: 'I would believe that 70-80% of it can be found online' and 'what I'm really paying for here is probably that last 10 or maybe at most 20%'
Not a price objection — he said the opposite: 'the $6,000, okay, fine. I don't have a problem with the price... I don't think that's too much by any means'

Overlaps substantially with the_rebuilder — eight months of decline after quitting his job, wants his former daily-gym self back, and carries visible regret about his father's decline — but the buying behaviour is governed by self-reliance as a principle, not by wanting rescue

goals.text: Just feel good again — functionality rather than size
Get into the best shape of his life by the time he turns 40 in two weeks
An anti-inflammatory diet and a meal plan someone else has already figured out
Stop ending up exhausted for a day after a two- or three-day hunting trip; be able to walk up a hill without his heart racing
Compete in a Tough Mudder obstacle event again, ideally annually
Clear the brain fog so he can study again and possibly start a YouTube channel
Keep up with his nieces and three nephews and be a present uncle in an 18-year window
Avoid ending his life in a nursing home unable to care for himself — 'so many people die at the age of 65, but they don't get buried till 85'
External accountability, which he named as the single biggest thing missing from his life

pains.text: Roughly 80% of his diet is DoorDash fast food at $30-35 a meal — 'I've turned into a DoorDash junkie the last six months'
Stopped caring about himself — 'I just don't give a crap about myself or anything. It's not that I'm depressed. I'm not depressed. I just stopped caring about a lot of things'
Heart racing after walking up a hill while hunting; had never experienced that before
Exhausted for a full day after hunting trips, to the point of not wanting to go
Brain fog for the last year or two in someone who describes himself as usually sharp
Could not keep up with his nieces during a two-week family visit and was teased by his younger brother for sleeping in
Stuck in a couch-potato habit loop deliberately started after quitting his job and never broken
Research paralysis on nutrition — too many conflicting options, has stopped watching videos because it is overwhelming
Intermittent right knee ache and persistent right elbow ache on gripping
Slight scoliosis producing a left-right strength imbalance
Watching his 65-year-old father — once extremely fit — decline into naps, medication and missing out on family trips
Sits at home most of the day after two or three hours of trading; drifting into video games

objections.raw_quote: It's going to be what I'm really paying for here is probably that last 10 or maybe at most 20% there that Trevor has an edge over other people... I would believe that 70-80% of it can be found online.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the information is all online, then reframed onto execution — 'there is a reason that you're still doing DoorDash at the moment. There's a reason that you haven't started yet in those months of doing research.' Genuinely the strongest move on the call, but it was made once and not built on.

objections.raw_quote: I don't even know if I really need the primal workout thing, or if I just want it at this point... if I need something, that thing becomes more valuable to me than something I just want... I'm not willing to pay six grand right now on just something I want.
objections.rep_response: Asked when he would be certain he could get there alone and pushed the pattern-break framing; did not dislodge it. Proposed label for this objection type: 'have_not_earned_help_yet' — a self-reliance principle rather than a price, value or timing objection.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I'm going to tell you right now, I'm not going to make a commitment on this call. I know that much.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it, agreed to stay in contact by phone and check in over the coming weeks with a review around two months out

objections.raw_quote: I'm paying for the accountability, but if I'm going to be my old self again, I don't need to be accountable to anybody. I've been accountable to myself my whole life.
objections.rep_response: Not addressed. The rep did not point out that forty minutes earlier the prospect had called accountability 'probably the biggest thing I need in my life'.

evidence: Explicit refusal on the call: 'I'm not going to make a commitment on this call. I know that much.'
Reasoned decline rather than a deferral: 'for $6,000, without me even really doing anything for myself, I can't justify that. It's a principal thing.'

'I have to give this a shot for myself and I'm either going to succeed and never talk to you again, or guess what? I'm going to fail... and I'm going to get ahold of you guys again in two or three months'

Counter-evidence for classifying this as lost: the door was left genuinely open, the prospect proposed the next meeting himself ('do we make a Zoom meeting for two months down the road?'), stated the price was fair, and said he would pay the $6,000 later if his own attempt stalls. Classified as lost rather than follow_up because a decision was made and it was no.
Counter-evidence on urgency: he has a hard self-imposed deadline of his 40th birthday in two weeks and said 'I'm going to do something with you guys or without you guys'
outcome.next_step: Rep to check in by phone over the coming weeks with a review around two months out; prospect attempts it on his own first

notable.note: Three things a principal should see. First, the prospect disclosed that he has 'stopped caring' about himself and the rep used that disclosure twice as a closing argument rather than acknowledging it. Second, the prospect spends roughly $30-35 per DoorDash meal on about 80% of his meals — an obvious affordability and cost-of-inaction anchor sitting in plain view that was never used. Third, and most consequential: the $1,000 self-serve tier was never mentioned to this prospect, even though he explicitly asked for a smaller first step and the same rep presented that tier to three other prospects in this same batch on adjacent days.
